course.title: Electrical Installation Basics
course.tagline: Wire lights, sockets and panels safely, and fault-find like a pro.

days.title: How Electricity Works in Your Home
days.goal: Follow electricity from the street pole to a socket in your home.

video.title: How Electricity Works in Your House (From the Pole to Your Outlet)

steps: Learn that power comes from the street into a meter, then to the main panel.
The main panel (also called a consumer unit) splits power into circuits.
Each circuit has a breaker that trips if too much current flows.
Draw the path from pole to meter to panel to socket.
days.task: Draw the path of electricity from the street to a socket.
days.challenge: Explain to a friend what a circuit breaker does.

quiz.q: Where does electricity enter a home?
options: From the street main into a meter, then the main panel
quiz.explain: Power comes from the street through the meter into the main panel.

quiz.q: What does a circuit breaker do?
options: Trips off when too much current flows
quiz.explain: A breaker is a safety switch that cuts power when a circuit is overloaded.

quiz.q: What is the main panel also called?
quiz.explain: The consumer unit (main panel) splits power into separate circuits.

days.title: Safety First: Never Work Live
days.goal: Learn the safety rules that keep you alive around electricity.

video.title: How Electricity Works in Your House (From the Pole to Your Outlet)

steps: Rule one: always switch off the power at the panel before you touch wires.
Test with a voltage tester to prove the wires are dead.
Tell someone you are working on the power.
Never work with wet hands or standing in water.
days.task: Write your own five safety rules and stick them above your bench.
days.challenge: Prove a circuit is dead using a tester, twice.

quiz.q: Where does electricity enter a home?

quiz.explain: Power comes from the street through the meter into the main panel.

quiz.explain: A breaker is a safety switch that cuts power when a circuit is overloaded.

quiz.q: What is the main panel also called?
quiz.explain: The consumer unit (main panel) splits power into separate circuits.

days.title: Tools and Testers
days.goal: Know the tools: screwdrivers, strippers, testers and pliers.

video.title: How Electricity Works in Your House (From the Pole to Your Outlet)

steps: Lay out insulated screwdrivers, wire strippers, a voltage tester and pliers.
Learn that insulated tools have plastic handles that protect you.
Practise stripping a wire: remove about 1cm of plastic without cutting the copper.
Test a known live socket with the tester, then a dead one.
days.task: Strip ten wire ends cleanly without nicking the copper.
days.challenge: Strip a wire to exactly the right length first try.

days.title: Wires: Live, Neutral and Earth
days.goal: Tell the three wires apart by colour and job.

video.title: How to Wire a Light Switch

steps: Live (brown or red) brings power in; neutral (blue or black) carries it back.
Earth (green and yellow, or bare copper) is the safety wire.
The earth wire gives fault current a safe path to the ground.
Open a plug and name each wire inside.
days.task: Open a plug and label the live, neutral and earth wires.
days.challenge: Name the three wires and their colours without looking.

quiz.q: What must you do before touching any wire?
options: Switch off the power and test that it is dead
quiz.explain: Switching off and testing dead is the only safe way to start.

quiz.q: What does a voltage tester do?
options: Shows if a wire is live or dead
quiz.explain: A tester tells you if power is present before you touch anything.

quiz.q: Why never work with wet hands on electrics?
options: Water conducts electricity and raises the shock risk
quiz.explain: Wet skin conducts electricity far better than dry skin.

days.title: Wire a Light Switch
days.goal: Wire a simple one-way light switch on a practice board.

video.title: How to Wire a Light Switch

steps: Switch the power off and prove it is dead.
Connect the live wire to one side of the switch and the switched live to the other.
Connect the earth wire to the earth terminal.
Switch the power on and test the light.
days.task: Wire a working light switch on a practice board.

video.title: How to Wire a Light Switch

steps: A one-way switch controls a light from one spot.
A two-way switch lets two switches control the same light, like a hallway.
Learn the terminals: COM (common), L1 and L2.

video.title: How to Wire an Electrical Outlet 2 Ways (Pigtails vs Daisy Chain)

Run wires from the supply to the switch, then to the bulb.

steps: Strip the wire ends cleanly.
Twist the copper ends together, then screw on a wire connector.
Tug each wire to check it is tight.
Cover the joint with tape and tuck it into a box.

video.title: How to Wire an Electrical Outlet 2 Ways (Pigtails vs Daisy Chain)

steps: Switch the power off and prove it dead.
Connect live to the brass screw, neutral to the silver screw, earth to the green screw.

days.title: Pigtails and Daisy Chains
days.goal: Wire sockets two ways: pigtails and daisy chains.

video.title: How to Wire a One Way Light Switch

steps: A pigtail is a short wire that joins one socket to the main wires.
A daisy chain runs the main wires from one socket to the next.
Learn why pigtails are safer: one loose socket cannot kill the rest.
Practise both ways on a board with two sockets.
days.task: Wire two sockets with a pigtail and two with a daisy chain.

days.goal: Wire a one-way switch neatly with the right cable.

video.title: How to Wire a One Way Light Switch

steps: Use twin and earth cable (two wires plus an earth in one sleeve).
Strip the outer sleeve without cutting the inner wires.
Connect live to COM and switched live to L1.
Neaten the cables with clips and test the switch.

days.title: Ring Circuits
days.goal: Understand a ring circuit: a loop of cable that feeds many sockets.

video.title: Ring Circuits Explained Step by Step

steps: A ring circuit is a loop that starts and ends at the panel.
The loop shares the load, so thinner cable can feed many sockets.
Learn that a break in the ring overloads the rest.
Draw a ring circuit feeding four sockets.
days.task: Draw a ring circuit with four sockets, labelled.
days.challenge: Explain why a ring must be a complete loop.

quiz.q: What is a ring circuit?
options: A loop of cable from the panel, through sockets, back to the panel
quiz.explain: A ring starts and ends at the panel, looping through the sockets.

quiz.q: Why is a ring circuit used for sockets?
options: The loop shares the load so many sockets can run safely
quiz.explain: The loop shares current between two paths, so more sockets can be fed.

quiz.q: What happens if a ring circuit breaks?
options: The rest of the ring can overload
quiz.explain: A break turns the ring into a radial, which can overload the cable.

days.goal: Wire two sockets on a board in a ring, and test them.

video.title: Ring Circuits Explained Step by Step

steps: Fix two sockets and a small panel to a board.
Run a ring of cable from the panel, through both sockets, back to the panel.
Connect every wire to the right terminal.

days.title: Radial Circuits
days.goal: Understand a radial circuit: one cable run from the panel to the sockets.

video.title: Ring Circuits Explained Step by Step

steps: A radial circuit runs in one line from the panel to the last socket.
It is simpler than a ring and used for smaller loads.
Learn the limit: a radial feeds fewer sockets than a ring.

days.challenge: Explain when to use a radial instead of a ring.

quiz.q: What is a radial circuit?
options: One cable run from the panel to the sockets in a line
quiz.explain: A radial runs in one line from the panel to the last socket.

quiz.q: When is a radial circuit a good choice?
options: For a small number of sockets or a single load
quiz.explain: Radials suit small loads, like one room or a single cooker.

quiz.q: How is a radial different from a ring?
options: It does not loop back to the panel
quiz.explain: A radial ends at the last socket; a ring returns to the panel.

quiz.q: Why wire lights with the loop-in method?

quiz.q: What should you do if a light stays on all the time?

quiz.q: How many switches can control one light with two-way wiring?

quiz.q: What is the first thing to check when a socket has no power?
quiz.explain: A tripped breaker is the most common cause of a dead socket.

quiz.q: How do you find a faulty appliance that trips a breaker?
options: Unplug everything, reset, plug back one by one
quiz.explain: Plugging back one at a time shows which item trips the breaker.

quiz.q: What is a short circuit?
options: A fault where live touches neutral or earth
quiz.explain: A short circuit is a low-resistance fault that causes a big current surge.
